description: Se 42 é a resposta para a Vida, o Universo e Tudo Mais, 4TREE é a pergunta que nasce na Terra, representa a conexão entre tecnologia e natureza: observar, conectar e transformar dados em decisões para fazer a agricultura crescer de forma mais inteligente. Reunindo conhecimentos em desenvolvimento de software, IoT, sistemas embarcados, eletrônica, sensores, análise de dados e agricultura.
summary:
SIRA: Bringing NASA Climate Intelligence to Family Farming
SIRA is an affordable agricultural decision-support system combining a low-cost IoT weather station with NASA Earth observation data to help small-scale farmers make informed crop rotation decisions.

The SIRA station monitors temperature, humidity, atmospheric pressure, light intensity, and UV radiation directly in the field. This data is integrated with NASA POWER information, including rainfall, wind speed, and historical climate records, creating a detailed climate profile for each plot. The system delivers simplified weekly mobile reports and practical crop rotation recommendations through a conversational chatbot.

How it addresses the challenge
The Field Shift challenge seeks tools combining NASA Earth observations and local data to improve crop rotation, soil health, and climate resilience. SIRA addresses this need by transforming environmental data into accessible agricultural guidance while preserving farmers' autonomy.

Why it is important
Millions of family farms lack affordable access to reliable, plot-level climate information. With an estimated production cost of R$400–R$600, SIRA offers an alternative to commercial weather stations costing over R$10,000. By democratizing climate intelligence, SIRA aims to reduce agricultural risks, support soil conservation, and build more resilient farming communities.
details:
SIRA is an agricultural decision support system that combines a low-cost IoT weather station with NASA orbital data.

The SIRA station, installed directly in the field, collects real-time temperature, air humidity, atmospheric pressure, luminosity, and UV radiation. This local data is merged with NASA POWER information (accumulated rainfall, wind speed, and climate history). The result is a microclimate profile specific to each agricultural area.

The system delivers:

  • Simplified weekly reports on mobile phones.
  • Conversational chatbot (via messaging app) that responds in the producer's language.
  • Practical crop rotation recommendations to protect the soil and improve income for the next harvest.

The hardware is designed to cost between R$400 and R$600, making monitoring accessible to family farming.

Benefits

  • Access to climate data by plot at a cost approximately 30 times lower than commercial stations.
  • Management and rotation decisions based on real information, not just calendars or intuition.
  • Simple interface (reports + chatbot), with no need to interpret complex graphs.
  • Possibility of recovering or improving low-productivity areas.
  • Open architecture, with direct integration to the NASA POWER API.

Intended Impact

Democratize the use of NASA data in the Brazilian agricultural sector, especially for family farmers and small producers who currently make crop decisions without reliable local climate history. The goal is to reduce climate risks, protect the soil throughout successive growing cycles, and increase the resilience and productivity of areas that currently operate "in the dark".

Tools, languages, hardware and software used

  • Hardware: Custom low-cost IoT station (SIRA) built around a Heltec development board for data processing and sensor integration.
  • Sensors: BME280 for air temperature, humidity, and atmospheric pressure; GUVA-S12SD for UV radiation; and BH1750 for light intensity.
  • Physical structure: A smartphone camera support rod adapted as the station's main support, combined with a plastic base designed to accommodate the electronic components.
  • Data: NASA POWER API + locally collected sensor data.
  • Interface: Weekly reports on mobile phones and chatbot via messaging app.
  • Architecture: Data fusion system (field sensors + satellite data) delivering agronomic recommendations.

Creative aspect

The main innovation lies in keeping the hardware extremely cheap without losing access to essential environmental information. Instead of trying to measure everything directly in the field (which would increase equipment costs), the team created a smart data-fusion approach: what the SIRA station measures locally is combined with what NASA provides through its climate database. The result is a more detailed climate profile for each agricultural area at a fraction of the traditional cost, delivered in a conversational and accessible way.

Factors considered by the team:

  • Economic reality of small producers (critical entry cost).
  • Limited connectivity in rural areas.
  • Need for simple and direct language (without complex dashboards).
  • Importance of maintaining farmer autonomy in final decisions.
  • Alignment with NASA's challenge of using Earth observations to support crop rotations that improve soil health and climate resilience.
  • Scalability and open architecture to facilitate adoption by cooperatives and technical assistance providers.
